reachable: Yes at the scored position, and the mechanism gets gradient in training. (1) The head module is registered as net.dualdisp_transport before make_opt(net.parameters(), steps), so all of its parameters are in the optimizer. (2) The injection reaches the scored read: wrap()'s _forward adds contrib to command positions 0..n-1 with n = min(n_cmd, (pred.size(1)+1)//2) = rmax+1, which covers every command index including the read at tok position 2*r; verified by execution on a probe-shaped odd-length layout (prediction at rpos moved by 0.070/0.081 once out_scale was made nonzero). The contribution is strictly causal — reads[i] is taken from the memory BEFORE the write at step i, the read gate is a function of the command alone, and at the read step the paired observation slot is zero/invalid so it writes nothing. stream.leakage_ok(net) still returns True after 60 steps of training in the displaced SAM regime. (3) Gradient reaches the new parameters: on real batches at init, grad norms were displace 8.01, path_key 3.40, src_ext 7.34, dst_ext 0.0 — exactly the ordering the hypothesis predicts ("displace moves first, then the extractor it reads from specialises"); after 30 real training steps dst_ext.grad is 4.6e-4, i.e. it comes alive once displace leaves zero. Init identity is exact and bitwise: kd == ks (torch.equal True), displace.weight all zero, out_scale all zero, dst_ext.bias == src_ext.bias, mean|dst_ext.weight - src_ext.weight| = 0.0160 (matches sym_init_noise 0.02). Muon routing is as claimed: path_key.weight and displace.weight are both (64,256), form a sibling pair, and route to _MuonKeys alongside the arch's six (64,176) addressing tensors; tr_read.weight is the (768,768) spectral-cap target. Full H._train runs clean end-to-end (40 steps normal, 60 steps with sam_warm_frac forced to 0 to exercise the displaced regime): ok=True, no non-finite parameters.
solves_outside_model: No. Both files import only math/torch — no json, no open(), no os, no string handling, no access to batch["cmds"] or any text field. The head reads only tok/types/key_pad/cmd_mask tensors and the arch's own modules. All mining is embedding geometry (squared-L2 duplicate distance on observation and command embeddings, counts of content-free steps), it selects TRAINING EXAMPLES and shapes a LOSS, and aux_loss is called only from evolve/harness.py:_train — never on the scoring path. Nothing resolves a move chain in Python, and nothing is stamped into a command token: the eval forward path sees only the memory the model built from its own learned keys and gates. The retracted-stream shape is not present here in any form. The optim is pure parameter arithmetic. The head's data claims are also true: I checked evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl and it is exactly 24 sequences, 8 images, 172 `mv` steps, every one exit 0 with empty output — the author measured what they could measure and labelled everything requiring torch as unmeasured.
summary:
The optim axis — the slot's assigned mechanism — does what it says, and I verified it by execution rather than reading. Relative SAM: the displacement is exactly rho*||W_p|| per tensor (measured ||eps||/||W|| = 0.02000 on every tensor), exactly along the gradient (cos(eps, grad) = +1.0000), scale-invariant to the harness's global grad clipping as claimed, zero during the 8% warmup, annealed linearly to zero, and exactly zero at t == steps so the scored weights are the clean iterate (sharp.displacement all-None after the final step). The spectral cap is applied to the clean iterate before the displacement, as stated. Training is stable in the displaced regime with no NaNs. Everything else in the optim is byte-identical to the parent's.

The head crossover is where the description outruns the code's effect. Of the four deltas from the parent (diff is clean and contains exactly these): the dual extractor with zero-init displacement is real and behaves exactly as specified, including the subtle gradient-ordering claim; pred_weight 0.25 -> 0.5 is a real change taken from the partner. But the two-pool mined-example cap — presented as one of three things "the combination computes that neither parent computes", with an explicit argument that the parent's rule starves deep chains — never executes: on the real root at the genome's real batch size the mined set is 139-176 pairs against a cap of 256, so candidate and parent keep hop-for-hop identical example sets on every batch I measured, including under the genome's own curriculum batcher at eight points across the 4000-step budget. And the n_cmd full-command scan, while correctly implemented and live in principle (the scoring stream is odd-length, contrary to the author's stated inertness condition), touches exactly 1 of 640 windows — a depth-1 window — and 0 of the 238 depth-3/4 windows that form the eligible slice.

So the honest account of this candidate is: parent + SAM + a dedicated destination-argument extractor + doubled prediction-supervision weight. Two of its four described head deltas are inert on this data. Nothing here reaches outside the model, nothing leaks, and the author was scrupulous about labelling unmeasured claims as unmeasured — the divergence is a false premise about the data, not a misrepresentation of the code.

divergences.claim: Head change (b): the two-pool mined-example cap is one of three things "the combination computes that neither parent computes". "The parent ranked the whole pool by exactness, which systematically prefers one-hop pairs (they are the cleanest duplicates) and starves the deep chains"; reserving a quota "keeps the key-alignment supervision alive AND puts depth-3+ chains into the read/prediction supervision."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The two-pool rule is implemented exactly as described, but it is dead code on the real training data: the cap NEVER binds, so candidate and parent keep the identical mined set, hop-for-hop. The parent therefore does not starve deep chains and the candidate rescues nothing.
divergences.evidence: Replayed the exact mining arithmetic (dup_o/dup_c/blank/hops/pair) on the real root /Users/fanzhu/PyCharmProjects/terminal-wm/data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd at the genome's real batch size (bs defaults to 64 in evolve/genome.py:26; the genome sets no 'bs'). Under the genome's own batcher (r6_sysblock_hardneg_curriculum) at steps 1/500/1000/2000/3000/3500/3900/4000 the mined-pair count was 159/169/166/158/171/173/158/164 — always below max_examples=256, so the `if bsel.numel() > cap` branch never executes. Ten contiguous 64-row batches gave 139-176. Over all 2304 training rows: mean 2.55 pairs/row, max 9/row. Side-by-side hop histograms under the parent rule and the candidate rule are byte-identical in every batch (TOTAL parent {1:624,2:374,3:73,4:159,5:58,6:122,7:78,8:116} == TOTAL cand). Only an adversarially chosen batch (the 64 highest-pair rows, 395 pairs) would trip the cap; the batcher does not produce one.

divergences.claim: Head change (c): "Both parents compute n = L // 2 ... so if the token stream ever ends with a command that has no paired observation token, the LAST command - the one being scored - is dropped ... it removes a mode in which the whole mechanism is switched off exactly at the position that is judged." Failure mode listed as: "If the scoring stream is always even-length, the n_cmd fix is inert."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The fix is implemented correctly and the stated premise is inverted — the scoring stream is ODD-length, not even (evolve/cups_probe.py:111, Lmax = 2*max(r)+1) — yet the effect on the scored slice is still nil, because only the single longest window in the batch has an unpaired trailing command; every shorter window's read sits at an interior, paired position.
divergences.evidence: On the inner-split cups context of the local root: 640 windows, Lmax=57 (odd), rmax=28, and exactly 1 window has r==rmax — that window is depth 1. Of the 238 depth-3/4 windows (the eligible slice), 0 have r==rmax. A synthetic 2-window layout does show the difference (parent head contributes |delta|=0.0 at the deepest window's read position, candidate 0.081), confirming the mechanism is real; it just has essentially no scored rows to act on. The author's conclusion ("can only help or do nothing") survives; the reasoning behind it does not.

divergences.claim: Optim: "eps_{t+1,p} = rho_t * ||W_p|| * g_{t+1,p} / ||g_{t+1,p}||   per parameter tensor p".
divergences.what_the_code_does: _RelativeSharpness.displace() reads p.grad, which is g_t — the gradient just consumed by the step, evaluated at w_t + eps_t. g_{t+1} does not exist yet at that point in the loop.
divergences.evidence: optim__r5_relsam_spectral_transport_keys.py, _SharpCapOpt.step(): restore(); adamw.step(); muon.step(); cap.project(); t+=1; displace() — and displace() uses `g = p.grad`, untouched by AdamW or _MuonKeys (both are out-of-place w.r.t. .grad). The very next sentence of the hypothesis states the code's actual behaviour correctly ("the ascent direction is the gradient at the previous perturbed iterate"), so this is an index slip in the formula, not a claim about different behaviour.

divergences.claim: "the SECOND command extractor ... so that the destination argument of a command has its own extraction pathway into the shared path-to-key encoder" (and the impl DESCRIPTION's "while the source key itself comes from one shared path-to-key encoder").
divergences.what_the_code_does: fd = gelu(dst_ext(c)) is fed to `displace`, NOT to `path_key`. path_key sees only the source features, so it is no longer shared between the two keys — only the additive base term is shared.
divergences.evidence: address(): `fs = gelu(src_ext(c)); fd = gelu(dst_ext(c)); base = path_key(fs); return unit(base), unit(base + displace(fd)), fs`. The hypothesis's own equation in section (a) states this correctly; only the prose bullet and the DESCRIPTION are loose. (The crossover partner r2_dualaddress_move_transport does route both extractors through path_key — kd = unit(path_key(gelu(dst_ext(c)))) — so the wording appears to be carried over from the partner.)

divergences.claim: DESCRIPTION: "every tensor is displaced ... so the next step's gradient is evaluated at the displaced point."
divergences.what_the_code_does: True for ~80% of the budget only. radius() returns 0 for t < warm (8% = 320 of 4000 steps) and anneals to 0 over the last 12%, hitting exactly 0 at t == steps.
divergences.evidence: Executed with steps=50: radius 0 at t=1..3, 0.02 at t=4..~43, 0.00333 at t=49, 0.0 at t=50, and sharp.displacement is all-None after the final step. The hypothesis body states the schedule explicitly, so this is a summary-level overstatement in the DESCRIPTION only.
